doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Starting violin and his father's Des Moines band
summary: Lanny began violin at six; his father played sax and led the WHO staff band, but his mother kept the horns out of the house.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yes I did. Where do you get your information?

I started violin when I was six years old. My dad was a saxophone player in Des Moines, Iowa. He traveled around the midwest with the band and he also had the staff band of WHO and this was when Ronald Reagan was the, Dutch Reagan was the sportscaster. My dad, who loved him immensely said he didn’t know anything about sports either. So anyway—
He was. It just proves that a bad actor can be a bad president.

But anyway my mother didn’t want him to bring his horns home because it was still during the depression and there was a lot of carousing and drinking and wild women going on and she wanted her little boy to be something better than that. So he complied with her wishes. He never brought his horns home and practiced. But in the sixth grade I came home with a violin and so it started then. I was into it.
